messages.content: Predict the person’s selection in a hypothetical autonomous-vehicle emergency. A self-driving car carrying one passenger travels at the speed limit on an urban road. After a traffic-light malfunction, three pedestrians cross into its path, two directly in front and a third just behind. There is no time to brake safely. The person judges which of three possible emergency outcomes is most appropriate. Actual steering manoeuvres are not specified; outcomes are stated as each of four people’s chance of survival. Percentages are survival probabilities, not money or realized deaths. No simulated crash is carried out and the participation fee does not depend on whom the person selects. Labels are neutral: outcome 1, outcome 2, outcome 3. The three questions appear in fixed order: first four unlabeled people, then passenger/pedestrian role labels, then one’s personal role is disclosed. Before disclosure the person has equal chance of being any of the four characters. At each question, use only information disclosed so far. They can read the scenario without a time limit. Personal age, gender and schooling describe the respondent outside the hypothetical scene; they do not identify any masked character. Output only 1, 2 or 3.
